{"world_model":"W1 (mechanism), after E007.

The setup
- The tip runs HYP epochs=10.0, but the idea texts say "9". With batch 2000 that is 25 steps per epoch and 250 steps in total.
- The resolution switch is keyed on epoch index (start × epochs), so the phases are 4 epochs at 24 px, 3 at 28 px and 3 at 32 px.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: same math, 14% faster (E002 → E004). E003's slowdown came from stride-guard recompiles leaking into timed code; E004 fixed it.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% extra time (E005).
  - The t^3 alpha ramp averages the last ~20% of noisy high-lr iterates, including the BN buffers. It acts like an extra anneal and is worth about 1.5 epochs.
- Muon on the conv filters (E006): +0.66 pp, about 4% slower at equal epochs.
  - Orthogonalized updates on fixed-norm filters give a better step per sample and work well at batch 2000.
  - The Newton-Schulz cost is small: the per-step overhead is a few ms, and fewer, larger steps offset it.
  - I under-forecast both the Muon and EMA gains. This recipe family has more accuracy headroom than I assumed.
- Progressive resizing (E007): −22% time, −0.59 pp.
  - Pixel-weighted cost is 0.754 of full resolution, and measured time fell to 0.776. So the run is mostly GPU/FLOP-bound, with small overhead.
  - Accuracy loses about 0.6 pp because:
    - fewer pixels means less information per sample;
    - there is a train/test scale mismatch, mitigated because the last 30% (and all of the EMA window) is at 32 px.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s (H2D copy, eigh, pad).
- The rest is per-step and roughly proportional to pixels × FLOPs: about 27 ms per step on average, and about 35 ms at 32 px.
- FLOP shares by group are roughly 20% / 50% / 32%. The last group runs at 7→3 px spatial, so narrowing it 576→512 saves only about 5% of FLOPs, or about 2-4% of time.
- CPU launch overhead is small at batch 2000, so CUDA graphs can gain only a few percent. They also carry risk (python-float lrs, optimizer outside the graph).

The accuracy model
- The slope is about 0.5-0.7 pp per epoch, i.e. 0.25-0.35 pp per 0.5 epoch.
- The tip is 0.6 pp above the bar, so cutting about 0.5-1 epoch is the obvious dial.
- A lower LR floor overlaps heavily with EMA, so I expect at most a small gain.
- Recomputing BN stats after EMA mostly duplicates the buffer averaging. Its gain is probably under 0.2 pp, and a new batch shape risks an autotune or recompile cost.

Noise
- 3-seed mean std is about 0.15-0.2 pp; time noise is about 1-2%.
- Compiled runs are probably not bit-identical: cuDNN benchmark and atomic adds in the weight-gradient kernels.
- For the 40-seed judgment, keep the 3-seed mean at 0.755 or above.

Unsure
- How literally the implementers will read "9 → 8.5" when the code says 10. A literal 8.5 is a 1.5-epoch cut and would likely fail the bar.
- The size of the Muon slope.

W1 (mechanism), after E007.

The setup
- The tip runs HYP epochs=10.0, but the idea texts say "9". With batch 2000 that is 25 steps per epoch and 250 steps in total.
- The resolution switch is keyed on epoch index (start × epochs), so the phases are 4 epochs at 24 px, 3 at 28 px and 3 at 32 px.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: same math, 14% faster (E002 → E004). E003's slowdown came from stride-guard recompiles leaking into timed code; E004 fixed it.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% extra time (E005).
  - The t^3 alpha ramp averages the last ~20% of noisy high-lr iterates, including the BN buffers. It acts like an extra anneal and is worth about 1.5 epochs.
- Muon on the conv filters (E006): +0.66 pp, about 4% slower at equal epochs.
  - Orthogonalized updates on fixed-norm filters give a better step per sample and work well at batch 2000.
  - The Newton-Schulz cost is small: the per-step overhead is a few ms, and fewer, larger steps offset it.
  - I under-forecast both the Muon and EMA gains. This recipe family has more accuracy headroom than I assumed.
- Progressive resizing (E007): −22% time, −0.59 pp.
  - Pixel-weighted cost is 0.754 of full resolution, and measured time fell to 0.776. So the run is mostly GPU/FLOP-bound, with small overhead.
  - Accuracy loses about 0.6 pp because:
    - fewer pixels means less information per sample;
    - there is a train/test scale mismatch, mitigated because the last 30% (and all of the EMA window) is at 32 px.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s (H2D copy, eigh, pad).
- The rest is per-step and roughly proportional to pixels × FLOPs: about 27 ms per step on average, and about 35 ms at 32 px.
- FLOP shares by group are roughly 20% / 50% / 32%. The last group runs at 7→3 px spatial, so narrowing it 576→512 saves only about 5% of FLOPs, or about 2-4% of time.
- CPU launch overhead is small at batch 2000, so CUDA graphs can gain only a few percent. They also carry risk (python-float lrs, optimizer outside the graph).

The accuracy model
- The slope is about 0.5-0.7 pp per epoch, i.e. 0.25-0.35 pp per 0.5 epoch.
- The tip is 0.6 pp above the bar, so cutting about 0.5-1 epoch is the obvious dial.
- A lower LR floor overlaps heavily with EMA, so I expect at most a small gain.
- Recomputing BN stats after EMA mostly duplicates the buffer averaging. Its gain is probably under 0.2 pp, and a new batch shape risks an autotune or recompile cost.

Noise
- 3-seed mean std is about 0.15-0.2 pp; time noise is about 1-2%.
- Compiled runs are probably not bit-identical: cuDNN benchmark and atomic adds in the weight-gradient kernels.
- For the 40-seed judgment, keep the 3-seed mean at 0.755 or above.

Unsure
- How literally the implementers will read "9 → 8.5" when the code says 10. A literal 8.5 is a 1.5-epoch cut and would likely fail the bar.
- The size of the Muon slope.
- Whether 20 px is too coarse: after the 2×2 whitening conv, the group-3 maps shrink to 2×2.

forecasts.reason: Cutting 0.5 epoch from 10 saves ~5% at −0.25-0.35 pp. If the implementer reads 8.5 literally (a 1.5-epoch cut), accuracy drops to about 0.751. Whether ≥0.756 holds is a coin flip.
EMA already removes the end-of-run iterate noise that a zero LR floor would remove. The gain is about +0.1 pp, below the 0.3 pp threshold.
Pixel cost falls about 15% versus E007, giving ~9% less time. 20 px loses another ~0.4-0.6 pp, so the result lands right at the bar.
The last group runs at tiny spatial size, so narrowing it saves ~5% of FLOPs and only ~2-4% of time, under the 4% bar. It costs ~0.2-0.3 pp.
The recipe is unchanged. For CIFAR-100 airbench-style runs, per-seed std is about 0.2-0.3 pp and the held-out mean should fall within 0.3 pp of the seeds 0-2 mean.
Batch-2000 steps are GPU-bound and launch overhead is a few ms per step. Graphs would save ~2-5%, with risks around lr tensors and capturing the optimizer.
The averaged BN buffers already roughly match the averaged weights, so recomputation gains under 0.3 pp. A new forward shape adds cuDNN-benchmark cost, likely about 0.1-0.2 s.

cruxes: What is the accuracy-vs-epochs slope with Muon + EMA + resizing on? It sets how much of the 0.6 pp margin converts to time: ~0.3 pp per 0.5 epoch would allow cutting about 1 epoch.
Is the per-step time FLOP-bound or launch-bound? E007 suggests ~90% FLOP-bound, which favours resolution and width cuts over CUDA graphs.

How much accuracy does a 20 px phase cost? Is the loss driven by early-phase information or by train/test scale mismatch? If the latter, keeping the EMA window at 32 px makes aggressive early downscaling nearly free.
